## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

1	/-

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic
7	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Pullbacks
8	
9	/-!
10	# The relative Picard functor of a curve
11	
12	For a scheme `C` over a field `k` (an object of `Over (Spec k)`) this file defines the
13	relative Picard functor of Grothendieck–Kleiman:
14	$$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(T) \;=\; \operatorname{Pic}(C \times_k T)\,/\,
15	  \operatorname{Pic}(T),$$
16	line-bundle classes on `C ⊗ T` modulo classes pulled back from the test object `T`
17	along the second projection. The quotient — never the absolute `Pic(C ⊗ T)`, which is
18	not even a separated presheaf in any useful sense — is the functor that étale
19	sheafification and the representability theorem consume.
20	
21	Products are the cartesian-monoidal product of `Over (Spec k)` (chosen pullbacks of
22	schemes): `C ⊗ T`, projection `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`, matching the vocabulary
23	of the challenge statement file.
24	
25	## Main declarations
26	
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase C T`: the subgroup of `(C ⊗ T).left.CechPic` of classes
28	  pulled back from `T` along the second projection.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPic C T`: the relative Picard group, the quotient by
30	  `picFromBase C T`, a `CommGroup`; `relPicMk` is the projection, with
31	  `relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff` the exact coset relation (a genuine range condition, no
32	  choice, no `Nonempty (≅)`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMap C g`: restriction along `g : T' ⟶ T`, descended from
34	  pullback of Čech classes along `C ◁ g`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicFunctor C`: the relative Picard functor
36	  `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
37	-/
38	
39	set_option autoImplicit false
40	
41	universe u
42	
43	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
44	open AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme (CechPic)
45	
46	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
47	
48	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
49	
50	noncomputable section
51	
52	/-- The subgroup of Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` pulled back from the test object `T`
53	along the second projection. The relative Picard group is the quotient by it. -/
54	def picFromBase (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup ((C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :=
55	  (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range
56	
57	lemma mem_picFromBase_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
58	    L ∈ picFromBase C T ↔ ∃ N : T.left.CechPic, CechPic.map (snd C T).left N = L :=
59	  Iff.rfl
60	
61	/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: Picard classes on `C ⊗ T`
62	modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
63	def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
64	  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ picFromBase C T
65	
66	noncomputable instance (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : CommGroup (relPic C T) :=
67	  QuotientGroup.Quotient.commGroup (picFromBase C T)
68	
69	/-- The projection from Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` to the relative Picard group. -/
70	noncomputable def relPicMk (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
71	    (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic →* relPic C T :=
72	  QuotientGroup.mk' (picFromBase C T)
73	
74	lemma relPicMk_surjective (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
75	    Function.Surjective (relPicMk C T) :=
76	  QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective (picFromBase C T)
77	
78	/-- The exact coset relation: two Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` have equal image in the
79	relative Picard group iff their ratio is pulled back from `T`. -/
80	lemma relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
81	    {L L' : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
82	    relPicMk C T L = relPicMk C T L' ↔ L / L' ∈ picFromBase C T :=
83	  QuotientGroup.eq_iff_div_mem
84	
85	@[elab_as_elim]
86	theorem relPic.ind {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {motive : relPic C T → Prop}
87	    (mk : ∀ L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic, motive (relPicMk C T L)) (x : relPic C T) :
88	    motive x :=
89	  QuotientGroup.induction_on x mk
90	
91	variable {T T' T'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
92	
93	/-- Pullback of Čech Picard classes along `C ◁ g` sends classes from `T` to classes
94	from `T'`: the well-definedness of `relPicMap` on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
95	lemma picFromBase_le_comap (g : T' ⟶ T) :
96	    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C T').comap (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) := by
97	  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩
98	  refine ⟨CechPic.map g.left N, ?_⟩
99	  show CechPic.map (snd C T').left (CechPic.map g.left N)
100	      = CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left (CechPic.map (snd C T).left N)
101	  rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
102	    ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left, ← Over.comp_left, whiskerLeft_snd]
103	
104	/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along `g : T' ⟶ T`: pull back along
105	`C ◁ g` and descend to the quotients. -/
106	noncomputable def relPicMap (g : T' ⟶ T) : relPic C T →* relPic C T' :=
107	  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C T')
108	    (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) (picFromBase_le_comap C g)
109	
110	@[simp]
111	lemma relPicMap_mk (g : T' ⟶ T) (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
112	    relPicMap C g (relPicMk C T L) = relPicMk C T' (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left L) :=
113	  QuotientGroup.map_mk' _ _ _ _ L
114	
115	lemma relPicMap_id (x : relPic C T) : relPicMap C (𝟙 T) x = x := by
116	  induction x using relPic.ind with
117	  | mk L =>
118	    rw [relPicMap_mk, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id, Over.id_left,
119	      Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
120	    rfl
121	
122	lemma relPicMap_comp (g : T' ⟶ T) (h : T'' ⟶ T') (x : relPic C T) :
123	    relPicMap C (h ≫ g) x = relPicMap C h (relPicMap C g x) := by
124	  induction x using relPic.ind with
125	  | mk L =>
126	    rw [relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk]
127	    refine congrArg (relPicMk C T'') ?_
128	    rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,
129	      ← MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp]
130	
131	/-- The relative Picard functor `T ↦ Pic(C ⊗ T)/Pic(T)` of Grothendieck–Kleiman, as a
132	presheaf of commutative groups on `Over (Spec k)`. -/
133	noncomputable def relPicFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
134	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (relPic C T.unop)
135	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (relPicMap C g.unop)
136	  map_id T := by
137	    ext x
138	    exact relPicMap_id C x
139	  map_comp g h := by
140	    ext x
141	    exact relPicMap_comp C g.unop h.unop x
142	
143	@[simp]
144	lemma relPicFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
145	    (relPicFunctor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (relPic C T.unop) :=
146	  rfl
147	
148	@[simp]
149	lemma relPicFunctor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
150	    (x : relPic C T.unop) :
151	    (relPicFunctor C).map g x = relPicMap C g.unop x :=
152	  rfl
153	
154	/-! ## Naturality in the curve -/
155	
156	variable {C} {C' C'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
157	
158	/-- Pullback of Čech classes along `g ▷ T` sends classes pulled back from `T` to classes
159	pulled back from `T`: well-definedness of the curve-direction map on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
160	lemma picFromBase_le_comap_whiskerRight (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
161	    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C' T).comap (CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left) := by
162	  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩
163	  refine ⟨N, ?_⟩
164	  show CechPic.map (snd C' T).left N
165	      = CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left (CechPic.map (snd C T).left N)
166	  rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,
167	    whiskerRight_snd]
168	
169	/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along a morphism of curves `g : C' ⟶ C`,
170	at a fixed test object: pull back along `g ▷ T` and descend to the quotients. -/
171	noncomputable def relPicMapCurveApp (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
172	    relPic C T →* relPic C' T :=
173	  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C' T)
174	    (CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left) (picFromBase_le_comap_whiskerRight g T)
175	
176	@[simp]
177	lemma relPicMapCurveApp_mk (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
178	    (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
179	    relPicMapCurveApp g T (relPicMk C T L)
180	      = relPicMk C' T (CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left L) :=
181	  QuotientGroup.map_mk' _ _ _ _ L
182	
183	/-- Naturality of the relative Picard functor in the curve: a morphism of curves
184	`g : C' ⟶ C` induces a natural transformation `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{C'/k}`. -/
185	noncomputable def relPicMapCurve (g : C' ⟶ C) :
186	    relPicFunctor C ⟶ relPicFunctor C' where
187	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (relPicMapCurveApp g T.unop)
188	  naturality T T' t := by
189	    ext x
190	    induction x using relPic.ind with
191	    | mk L =>
192	      show relPicMapCurveApp g T'.unop (relPicMap C t.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L))
193	          = relPicMap C' t.unop (relPicMapCurveApp g T.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L))
194	      rw [relPicMap_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMap_mk]

12	(`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §2 (N4)/(N5), GAP-3 companion)
13	
14	This file provides the module-theoretic heart of the canonical-section normalization —
15	the deferred GAP-3 **Nakayama companion** (I-0253): a *given* fibrewise-nonzero element of
16	a rank-`1` finite projective module is a **Zariski-local basis** (the converse direction
17	of N3's generator production) — together with the DAT-A class law N4 for arbitrary
18	fibrewise-regular sections of the divisor datum.
19	
20	* `Module.exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton` — **the Nakayama companion** (GAP-3
21	  companion, deferred from C2/I-0253): for a finite projective `B`-module `Q` of
22	  stalk-rank `1` at `p` and an element `q` nonzero in the fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p)`, there is a
23	  basic open `D(f) ∋ p` on which `x ↦ x • q` is a **bijection** `B_f → Q_f`, i.e. `q`
24	  is a local basis of `Q`.  Route: over the local ring `Rₚ` the localized module `Qₚ` is
25	  free of rank `1`; the fibre nonzeroness pins the basis coordinate of `q` to a unit, so
26	  `q` spans `Qₚ`; `PicardGroup`'s `bijective_of_surjective` (invertible target) upgrades
27	  spanning to bijectivity, and `Module.FinitePresentation.exists_notMem_bijective` spreads
28	  the stalk bijection to a basic open.
29	* `Module.exists_notMem_smul_eq_of_tmul_ne_zero` — **the local-rescaling corollary** (the
30	  N5 engine input): a second element `q'` lies in the `B_f`-span of the local basis `q`,
31	  so `q' = a • q` in `Q_f` for a scalar `a`.

33	Consumers: N5 (the relative uniqueness / mono engine) and the §3.2 chart mono
34	consume the local basis to rescale the two canonical sections by a unit

49	/-- **The Nakayama companion — a fibrewise-nonzero element is a Zariski-local basis**
50	(worksheet GAP-3 companion, deferred from C2/I-0253): for a finite projective `B`-module
51	`Q` of stalk-rank exactly `1` at the prime `p`, an element `q : Q` whose image in the
52	fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p)` is nonzero generates `Q` freely on a basic open `D(f) ∋ p`: the map
53	`x ↦ x • q` is a bijection `B_f → Q_f`.
54	
55	Over the local ring `Rₚ` the localized module `Qₚ` is free of rank `1`, so `q`'s basis
56	coordinate `c` satisfies: if `c` were a non-unit it would lie in the maximal ideal, hence
57	`q` would vanish in the fibre `κ(p) ⊗ Qₚ ≅ Q ⊗ κ(p)`, contradicting `hq`. Thus `c` is a
58	unit and `q` spans `Qₚ`; `Module.Invertible`'s `bijective_of_surjective` promotes spanning
59	to a bijection, and the isomorphism spreads to a basic open. -/
60	theorem exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton
61	    [Module.Finite B Q] [Module.Projective B Q] (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
62	    (hrank : Module.rankAtStalk Q p = 1) (q : Q)
63	    (hq : (q ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) : Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
64	    ∃ f : B, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ Function.Bijective
65	      (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f) (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q)) := by
66	  classical
67	  haveI : Module.FinitePresentation B Q := Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B Q
68	  set Rₚ := Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal with hRₚ
69	  set Qₚ := LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q with hQₚ
70	  set mkq : Qₚ := LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q q with hmkq
71	  -- `Qₚ` is finite, flat and hence free of rank `1` over the local ring `Rₚ`
72	  haveI : Module.Free Rₚ Qₚ := Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing
73	  have hrank1 : Module.finrank Rₚ Qₚ = 1 := hrank
74	  -- a basis of the free rank-`1` module, and the coordinate of `mkq`
75	  set b : Module.Basis Unit Rₚ Qₚ := Module.basisUnique Unit hrank1 with hb
76	  set c : Rₚ := b.repr mkq default with hc
77	  have hmkq_eq : mkq = c • b default := by
78	    have hsum := b.sum_repr mkq
79	    rw [Fintype.sum_unique, ← hc] at hsum
80	    exact hsum.symm
81	  -- `c` is a unit: otherwise `mkq` vanishes in the fibre, contradicting `hq`
82	  have hcunit : IsUnit c := by
83	    rw [← IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal]
84	    intro hcmem
85	    -- the fibre map `κ ⊗[Rₚ] Qₚ → κ ⊗[B] Q` sends `1 ⊗ mkq` to `1 ⊗ q`, injectively
86	    set κ := p.asIdeal.ResidueField with hκ
87	    set η : Qₚ ≃ₗ[Rₚ] Rₚ ⊗[B] Q := LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q
88	      with hη
89	    set ε : κ ⊗[Rₚ] Qₚ →ₗ[Rₚ] κ ⊗[B] Q :=
90	      (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange B Rₚ κ κ Q).toLinearMap.restrictScalars Rₚ
91	        ∘ₗ (η.lTensor κ).toLinearMap with hε
92	    have hηmkq : η mkq = (1 : Rₚ) ⊗ₜ[B] q := by
93	      rw [hη, hmkq, LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap_apply,
94	        LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct_apply_mk, Localization.mk_one]
95	    have hεval : ε ((1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[Rₚ] mkq) = (1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[B] q := by
96	      simp only [hε, LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
97	        LinearEquiv.lTensor_tmul, hηmkq,
98	        TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange_tmul, one_smul]

100	    have hcres : c • (1 : κ) = 0 := by
101	      rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one, IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebraMap_eq]
102	      exact (IsLocalRing.residue_eq_zero_iff c).mpr hcmem
103	    have hzero : (1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[Rₚ] mkq = 0 := by
104	      rw [hmkq_eq, ← TensorProduct.smul_tmul, hcres, TensorProduct.zero_tmul]
105	    -- transport the vanishing to `Q ⊗ κ`, contradicting `hq`
106	    have h1q : (1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[B] q = 0 := by rw [← hεval, hzero, map_zero]
107	    exact hq (by
108	      rw [show (q ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : κ) : Q ⊗[B] κ)
109	          = TensorProduct.comm B κ Q ((1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[B] q) from rfl, h1q, map_zero])

section AbelAff

variable (C) in
/-- **The Abel transformation of a widened locally certified class at an affine test**: the
étale-unit image of the relative Picard class of `𝒪(F₀)`.

Verbatim `abelDivPlus` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean`) with `DivFamZarAff` in place of
`DivFamZar` — the class map `DivFamZarAff.picClass` is all that is consumed, and it never saw
the cover, so no chart typing enters. -/
def abelDivAffPlus (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (F₀ : DivFamZarAff C A n) :
    PicEtAff C A :=
  PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) F₀.picClass)

/-- **Naturality of the widened affine Abel transformation in the test algebra**
(`DivFamZarAff.picClass_mapAlg` + `PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit`): base change of the widened Abel
value is the Abel value of the base-changed class. -/
theorem abelDivAffPlus_mapAlgHom {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra k B] (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) (F₀ : DivFamZarAff C A n) :
    PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ (abelDivAffPlus C A F₀)
      = abelDivAffPlus C B (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φ F₀) := by
  letI : Algebra A B := φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
  haveI : IsScalarTower k A B := .of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (φ.commutes a).symm
  have hclass : (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φ F₀).picClass
      = Scheme.CechPic.map (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left F₀.picClass := by
    have hcurve : relCurveMap C A B = (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left := by
      refine congrArg (fun ψ : overSpec k B ⟶ overSpec k A => (C ◁ ψ).left) ?_
      exact Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl
    rw [← hcurve]
    exact DivFamZarAff.picClass_mapAlg B n F₀
  calc PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ (abelDivAffPlus C A F₀)
      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicAlgMap C φ
          (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) F₀.picClass)) := PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit C φ _
    _ = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B)
          (Scheme.CechPic.map (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left F₀.picClass)) :=
        congrArg (PicEtAff.unit C B)
          (relPicMap_mk C (Over.overSpecMap φ) F₀.picClass)
    _ = abelDivAffPlus C B (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φ F₀) := by
        rw [abelDivAffPlus, hclass]

omit [IsProper C.hom] in
/-- **The widened hook extends the chart-typed one along `DivFamZar.toAff`**: the widened Abel
value of the image of a chart-typed class is the chart-typed Abel value.

This is what makes the file an *extension* of `Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean` rather than a second,
incompatible Abel layer: `DivFamZarAff.picClass_toAff` says the widening does not move the
Picard class, and both hooks are `unit ∘ relPicMk` of that class. -/
theorem abelDivAffPlus_toAff {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] (F₀ : DivFamZar C A π n) :
    abelDivAffPlus C A F₀.toAff = abelDivPlus C π A F₀ := by
  rw [abelDivAffPlus, abelDivPlus, DivFamZarAff.picClass_toAff]

end AbelAff
